title: Made a Warlock-style browser arena with Claude Code. It even cut its own trailer, which was weird
author: ScaredAudience4
selftext:
So I've been building a browser game with Claude Code and wanted to share where it ended up, plus a few things that surprised me.

It's called Spellmoot. 2-8 wizards on a small island, lava rising around it, and you try to knock each other in. If you played Warlock in Warcraft 3 back in the day, yeah, it's that. I missed it.

I didn't write the code. I told Claude what I wanted and argued with it a lot. Server, client, netcode, tests, all of it. Plain JavaScript, no engine. Art is from a local image-to-3D setup rendered to sprites, sounds are recorded samples, trailer music is Suno.

Stuff I didn't see coming:

The wizard looked stiff and my first instinct was to blend the animation frames. Bad idea. I ended up with a see-through copy of myself trailing behind for a split second. What actually fixed it was just rendering more directions. Boring answer.

Sound was rough. The AI can't hear anything, so it was picking audio files more or less blind. I kept having to say things like "the countdown is annoying" and "why does picking a card sound like a door hinge". Took three rounds to get it decent.

Bots are great for finding broken stuff and useless for judging balance. They told me one spell won 71% of the time, fair enough. They also told me the swap spell is garbage, which it isn't, they just have no idea how to use it.

Also the bots looked like bots. Their aim was twitching like crazy. We "fixed" it once and it still twitched. Turned out the aim was fine, the thing they were aiming at was jumping around.

And the trailer. I didn't open a video editor. It recorded some bot matches, picked the good moments, did the camera and cut it to the music on its own. I mostly sat there. Still not sure how I feel about that.

Anyway it's live and basically nobody plays it yet, so every match is me and three bots. If you try it, grab a friend, it's just a link.

[spellmoot.com](http://spellmoot.com), needs keyboard and mouse, no signup

Ask me whatever.
